done_when: When close's merge of the default branch leaves the branch's own changes (its diff against the merge base) unchanged, the last review and its dismissals still count, and --dismiss given in the same command applies to that review; any change to the branch's own diff still needs a new review. New and existing repos: same behaviour in any repo on this release. One command-level test: review, dismiss, main moves, close merges it and the dismissal still holds without a new review.

findings.body: This replaces the fingerprint stored in `review.changed`, but the required checker still uses the old algorithm. `.github/workflows/forge.yml:31` checks out the PR base and line 41 installs Forge from that checkout; `src/forge/prcheck.py:176` then compares the recorded fingerprint with its own calculation. The supplied base's raw source confirms it hashes paths and HEAD blobs, whereas this branch hashes raw diff entries. Consequently, a review produced by this branch's close command is rejected as out of date by its required PR check, and another close cannot resolve it. Preserve compatibility with that checker during the transition. The command tests mock green GitHub checks, so they do not catch this mismatch.
findings.title: Preserve compatibility with the default-branch PR checker

findings.body: Raw output still honors `diff.orderFile`; sorting the pathspec arguments does not sort the returned records. Read-only Git checks against this branch confirmed that ordering `src/forge/templates/skill.md` first reverses the two raw records without changing any paths, modes or blob IDs. Changing this display preference therefore invalidates an unchanged review and rejects same-command dismissals at `src/forge/close.py:99`. A coordinator's local ordering preference can also make its fingerprint disagree with the PR check's default ordering. Disable configured ordering or canonicalize the raw records before hashing.
findings.title: Canonicalize raw diff ordering before hashing

why: After forge close merges the latest default branch, a review and the coordinator's dismissals stop counting even when the branch's own changes are unchanged, so a full review runs again and raises the same findings
